blockers.problem: AC1 'the first blocking answer passes through': every merge case has a single blocker; mutant merge() iterating reversed(results) (last blocker wins) survives verify_itd_dispatch (79/79) and verify_all_hard_gate_host_parity (133/133). Need a case with two blocking hooks asserting the first one's bytes.

AC1 'a crash of the dispatcher itself ... stays silent elsewhere': the in-process crash tests cover only PreToolUse and SubagentStop; mutant answer() failing closed as PreToolUse for every event (deny on Stop/UserPromptSubmit/PostToolUse) survives both suites. Need a dispatcher-crash case on Stop or UserPromptSubmit that expects exit 0 and empty stdout.

AC4 'a body with a here-document keeps the fail-closed sentinel': removing the '<<' check in _substitution_end survives verify_predeploy_independent_review and verify_predeploy_gate; the heredoc test string also contains a transport that another layer denies. Probe: under the mutant `echo $(cat <<EOF
'
EOF
rsync -a . h:/srv
')` loses the sentinel and the rsync invocation.

AC4 'case keeps the sentinel': removing the CASE_WORD_RE check survives both predeploy suites; under the mutant `echo $(case x in x) rsync ...;; esac)` gives no sentinel and no rsync invocation from _split_invocations, so the existing case test does not pin the claim.

AC4 'backtick keeps the sentinel': removing the backtick-inside-double-quotes check in _substitution_end survives both predeploy suites (the sentinel is lost for `echo "$(echo "`echo )`" rsync ...)"`); the existing case covers only an unquoted backtick inside $().

AC2 'a repeated sync changes nothing': only settings.json is compared byte for byte; a mutant sync writing a fresh timestamp into hooks/claude-dispatch.json on every run survives verify_hook_selection, verify_hooks_autoinstall and verify_sync_manifest. The routing table and itd-bytecode.json after a second sync are not checked.

AC2 'compiles the bytecode with the interpreter of the hooks': no check compares the cacheTag in itd-bytecode.json with sys.implementation.cache_tag of the registered interpreter, so a sync compiling with a different interpreter (the Windows case) would not fail any test.
